To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interface quality of atomic-layer deposited disordered Hf O2 on n- and on p-type silicon substrated is determined by the density of defects located in the bandgap, and by the density of interface states located close to the majority carrier band-edge.
the quality of the oxide/semiconductor interface is not affected by the processing conditions, and the charge trapping takes place mainly between the silicon and the oxide.
the interface quality of HfO2 films on silicon can be improved by increasing the growth temperature and the oxygen partial pressure.

the interface properties of atomic-layer deposited HfO2 films on n-type and p-type silicon.
the interface properties of HfO2 films deposited by ALD on n- and P-type Si(100) substrates at different growth temperatures and using different-precursors partial pressures.

the electrical-interface quality of the oxide on both p- and n-silicon substrates was good, and that the processing parameters did not affect the electrical interface quality significantly.
the electrical-interface quality of HfO2 films is comparable with that of thermal-oxide films.
the electrical quality of as-growth atomic-layer deposited disordered Hf O2 on p- or n-type silicon is comparable with that of thermal SiO2 on silicon.

the quality of the interface was comparable with the best results obtained for thermal oxides.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrical-interface quality of HfO2 films deposited by atomic layer deposition on n-type silicon is comparable to that of HfOx films deposited using other techniques on n-type silicon.

the electrical-interface quality of HfO2 is not strongly dependent on the growth conditions, and that the interface trap density is not a limiting factor for the electrical quality of this high-k dielectric.
